cover.headline: From the forest to our homes

headlines.c4: Fires cost Canada at least $3 billion a year
headlines.c6: Provinces are not ready for seasons like these
headlines.c8: Catch fires while they are small

lines.c1: About the size of Germany, and more than double any four years since 1990.
lines.c2: Summers ran 1.5°C above 1961 to 1990, and warming is linked to 1 in 3 hectares burned.
lines.c3: Health Canada estimates 1.1 million days of asthma symptoms in children in 2023.
lines.c4: Firefighting is most of it, and in four provinces it nearly doubled after 2022.
lines.c5: That is 870 million tonnes of greenhouse gases, which Canada tracks outside its official total.
lines.c6: They budget for mild fire seasons, fly old planes and borrow crews.
lines.c7: New planes, crews and a fire-watching satellite are due from 2026 into the 2030s.
lines.c8: In 2026, 7 in 10 hectares burned in fires that grew past 1,000 hectares within three days.
